Selected in 2003 by horticulturists Lauren Springer and Scott Ogden from a vigorous wild population in north-central Texas, Undaunted is a 2014 Plant Select winner valued for extending true pink muhly grass color into colder zones than the straight species can reliably handle. Its fine, mid-green, sometimes curling foliage forms a rounded mound that erupts in early fall into a haze of bright reddish-pink seed heads, fading to warm tawny brown through winter. It is markedly more cold-hardy and adaptable than the straight species, with strong deer resistance and virtually pest-free performance once established.

planting.note: Plant in full sun with consistently moist, well-drained soil, well suited to containers and the front of small borders; appreciates supplemental watering during dry spells.

Introduced by Brent Horvath of Intrinsic Perennial Gardens from a seedling of the popular cultivar Hameln, Piglet is even smaller than its already-compact parent, forming a tight mound of soft, fine-textured green foliage. In late summer it produces silvery to pinkish-white, bottlebrush-shaped flower spikes that stand just above the foliage and persist into fall. Its diminutive size, typically under 2 feet tall and wide, makes it one of the smallest garden fountain grass selections available, useful where even Little Bunny or Hameln would be too large.
